sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Xbox's Project Helix "is not a PC that can also play console games"
sources.text: Next Xbox console is "designed to be the ultimate gaming machine" by removing the "arbitrary constraints between console and PC games" Xbox VP of Next Generation Jason Ronald has clarified that Project Helix is "designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games, not a PC that can also play console games." In the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine , Ronald described Project Helix as "the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed." "The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed Project Helix's console and PC compatibility in March, adding that the console will "lead in performance" for Xbox and PC games. As Ronald previously discussed at GDC Festival of Gaming , Project Helix will utilise neural rendering, which uses AI models to enhance graphics. Ronald identified neural rendering as a particular focus for Project Helix, as it also addresses the ongoing component crisis. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and platform designer, it's one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also [making] things accessible and affordable." "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower [and] additional memory." He concluded: "I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last ten years." Reports last month indicated that Project Helix is expected to launch during the 2028 holiday season , with a projected price between $1,200 and $1,800.

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Microsoft Says Of The Next Xbox: ‘Helix Is A Console Capable Of Playing PC Games’
sources.text: Microsoft has put out an online magazine to celebrate 25 years of Xbox , and unquestionably to attempt even more damage control after a gruesome year of studio closures and mass layoffs. Within all the huff and puff lies a surprise: seven pages’ coverage of Project Helix, the codename for the next Xbox console. Within this is revealed the plan for Helix to be able to play games and even progress from every previous Xbox generation, as well as removing “the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.” So, asks the magazine and indeed us, “is Project Helix a console or a PC?” The answer is very definitively: a console. Sort of. The current generation of consoles were notably described ahead of launch as being far more like PCs in a sealed box than the traditional console designs of yore, and this appears to be something Microsoft is looking to get away from this time out. The emphasis here is on the so-called instantaneous nature of a console. Jason Ronald is Xbox’s VP of “next generation,” and is quoted saying, “When I think about what makes a console magical, it’s that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don’t have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings.” Which is…a bold claim, given anyone who owns an Xbox will know about having to install the latest updates, waiting for game patches to excruciatingly slowly download without taking advantage of your 1TB ethernet connection, or that unbearable pause each time you load it up for it to fill in the dashboard. But of Project Helix, Ronald says, “it’s really designed to be the ultimate gaming machineâone that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I’m able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly,” adding, “We’re very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games.” However, it’s hard to know just how clear this distinction is from Ronald’s very next words. “But if you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.” So it is a PC then? So confused. Other comments from Ronald include that “We don’t think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metricsâit’s really about gameplay innovation.” He adds, “It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways.” Which all rather seems to be laying the ground for a machine that’s not focusing on the very latest and most expensive chipsets, but rather one that’ll take advantage of the more recent progress in upscaling and the like, perhaps to prevent the machine costing an absolute fortune? This topic isn’t ignored. Describing it as a factor “the team couldn’t have foreseen when Project Helix began,” the component crisis gets a mention. “Meeting this challenge has become a primary driver of Helix’s innovation,” says the article. Ronald is quoted once more. “It’s definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it’s also one of the most exciting times because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable.” This, he says, is why there’s the focus on neural rendering, adding, “I think you’re going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you’ve seen in the last 10 years.” It’s all a lot of words to avoid pointing out that Microsoft itself is one of the primary causes of the crisis in the first place, one arm taking all the available components from the other in order to power its AI hubris. Beyond this, the piece delivers some very confusing messaging regarding Xbox’s current desperate rebranding. After a disastrous attempt to call everything from your console to your toaster “an Xbox,” the recent emphasis has been to return to the core idea of the Xbox itself, yet that message gets very lost in Microsoft’s own marketing. We’re told at once that this is all about “the Return of Xboxâthe return of a console,” and then that “Project Helix aims to take a wrecking ball to the dividers currently keeping players and their games apart,” quoting Ronald saying Helix is about “enabling [players] to experience those games wherever they choose to play. It’s about removing barriers to play, removing friction, and those arbitrary boundaries that have existed in the past.” So which is it? There are claims the new UI will adapt to whether the Xbox is being played on the living room TV, or streamed to a mobile device or a PC with mouse and keyboard. This really does sound like a confusion of previous messaging crashing into the current reverse-ferret. There’s no word one when we can expect to see Project Helix in more detail, and certainly nothing on an intended release date. It seems that Microsoft and Sony are currently playing chicken on revealing whether they’re aiming for 2027 or 2028, or perhaps even later given the tumult in the hardware industry. But at least we know it’s a console, not a PC, but also like a PC, and can be streamed to your mobile, or played on PC, and has all of the annoying complexity of PCs taken away, but also still there. sources.title: The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time
sources.text: "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering." Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable. The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday , and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games. "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation. "It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering." While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future , saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future. The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld . "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players." Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

sources.title: Xbox afirma que Project Helix é um console capaz de rodar jogos de PC — e não o contrário
sources.text: A Microsoft divulgou novos detalhes sobre o Project Helix, seu console de nova geração, e reforçou a ideia de que o videogame é capaz de rodar jogos de PC — mas não um PC que consegue rodar jogos de console. Em entrevista publicada na revista especial de 25 anos do Xbox, Jason Ronald, vice-presidente da próxima geração da marca, explicou que o projeto foi desenvolvido para funcionar como um console tradicional, e não como um computador com recursos de videogame. “O Helix foi projetado para ser um console capaz também de rodar jogos do seu PC. Não é um PC que também roda jogos de console”, afirmou Ronald. O executivo também destacou que o aparelho pretende eliminar barreiras entre as bibliotecas de jogos de PC e Xbox, na intenção de manter a experiência simples e intuitiva para os jogadores. Segundo Ronald, a proposta do Project Helix é reunir diferentes bibliotecas em um único dispositivo e permitir com que os jogadores acessem seus títulos com mais facilidade. O console também deve oferecer compatibilidade com quatro gerações de jogos e preservar o progresso das contas Xbox. O executivo explicou que a experiência poderá ser adaptada a diferentes perfis de jogadores. Quem preferir uma experiência tradicional terá acesso rápido aos jogos, enquanto usuários mais avançados poderão personalizar configurações e opções de desempenho. “Quando penso no que torna um console mágico, é o fato de ele tornar meus jogos instantaneamente acessíveis e prontos para jogar”, afirmou Ronald. Ele também destacou que os jogadores não precisarão se preocupar com atualizações de drivers ou configurações típicas de um PC. A ideia, segundo o executivo, é criar uma plataforma que reúna a praticidade dos consoles com a flexibilidade dos computadores. “Quando pensamos no Project Helix, ele foi realmente concebido para ser a máquina de jogos definitiva — uma que remove todas as barreiras de jogo que existiram historicamente”, declarou. Durante a entrevista, Ronald também comentou sobre os desafios de desenvolver um novo console em meio à crise de componentes de PC. Segundo ele, a Microsoft está investindo em tecnologias como a renderização neural para melhorar o desempenho sem exigir mais poder computacional ou memória. “É definitivamente um momento desafiador, mas, como designer de sistemas e plataformas, também é um dos momentos mais empolgantes”, afirmou. O executivo explicou que a equipe busca novas soluções para avançar tecnologicamente e, ao mesmo tempo, manter os custos de produção e os preços sustentáveis. Ronald citou a renderização neural como uma das principais apostas para a próxima geração. A tecnologia pode abranger diferentes técnicas de processamento de imagem, como aprimoramento de resolução, geração de quadros e reconstrução de iluminação, embora a Microsoft ainda não tenha detalhado como pretende aplicá-la no Project Helix. O executivo também afirmou que a próxima geração não deve ser definida apenas por especificações tradicionais — como resolução 8K ou taxas de atualização de 240 Hz. Para ele, o foco estará em novas experiências de jogo, maior imersão e avanços visuais mais eficientes. E você, está ansioso para conhecer a próxima geração de consoles? sources.name: IGN
sources.title: GTA 6 Global Release Times Confirmed: Here's How to Play Early Via the New Zealand Trick
sources.text: GTA 6 will have a regional release, which means certain people can actually play it early thanks to what's called the New Zealand trick. Rockstar Games has confirmed that GTA 6 will become available at midnight local time, as the clock strikes November 19, meaning some parts of the world will get the game earlier than others. Xbox has a pretty well-known loophole known as the New Zealand trick, which allows you to play games a full day early with ease. All you have to do is open your Xbox's settings menu, scroll down to System, and click on Language and location. Change the location tab to New Zealand and hit the "Restart Now" button on the right-hand side of this menu to reset your console. When you come back online, your console will be "in" New Zealand. As a result of this, make sure to buy GTA 6 before you change your console's location; otherwise, you will have to pay in New Zealand currency. As for PlayStation, there is also a New Zealand trick, but it's not nearly as easy or convenient. You have to create a new account based in New Zealand and buy a copy for that account. You can then enable game sharing to give the game back to your main account, but you will likely need to play the game on the New Zealand profile until it unlocks for your regular account. So, it may be too much of a headache to even bother with this on PS5. For those in the United States, using the New Zealand trick lets you play GTA 6 almost a full day early, at around 7am ET on November 18. This trick applies to those outside of the United States as well, but folks in the U.S. will arguably get the most mileage out of this, and playing early will help with the inevitable spoiler problem as GTA 6 goes live around the world ahead of you. If you're avoiding the New Zealand trick, you'll need to wait until midnight local time. As is well documented, GTA 6 is not being released on-disc. Rockstar Games has released a 'code-in-box' version that is available now. So, all will have to download GTA 6, which weighs in at 212GB. Rockstar will sell a double-sided map/poster for 99 cents on its online store. It will also be included for free with purchases from the company's store, but fans can also download and print out a free one as well if they want. While you wait for GTA 6 to unlock we've got loads of great coverage for you to check out, including Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research , and How Gaming's Top Content Creators Are Preparing for GTA 6's Launch and Beyond . Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

sources.title: How to Play GTA 6 Early on PS5 With New Zealand Trick—All Time Zones, Explained
sources.text: After years of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally within reach. Rockstar Games’ long-awaited sequel is set to become the biggest launch in video game history, with millions of players expected to jump in during its opening days. Needless to say, the hype is very real, and the wait is almost over. But what if you don’t want to wait for your local release time? If you’re hoping to get into GTA 6 as early as possible on PlayStation 5, you’ll want to know about the so-called ‘New Zealand trick’. In this guide, I’ll walk you through exactly how it works and explain each step you need to follow to try and access the game at the earliest possible opportunity. Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming out on November 19, unlocking at midnight local time around the world. That means that some territories will be able to access the game ‘earlier’ than others, thanks to how time zones work. New Zealand is always the first territory to access new games because of where it’s situated on the planet. Isn’t that lovely for them? But you can use a (relatively) easy trick to play GTA 6 early on PS5 by using this New Zealand method to unlock the game 12 or 13 hours earlier than usual. The problem is that PlayStation makes the trick a bit of a hassle, since you have to jump through a few hoops to get GTA 6 early on PS5. It’s not as easy as it is to do the New Zealand trick on XBOX , where you just need to flip a switch in the console’s settings menu. Here are the steps to follow to unlock GTA 6 early on PlayStation 5: But there’s an extra step you can consider… There’s an additional step to consider if you want to play GTA 6 on your own account as opposed to the New Zealand account. When you come to the second step after making a New Zealand-based PSN account, you’ll want to head to your console settings, then to Users and Accounts, then Other, then Console Sharing and Offline Play, and flick that over to ‘enable’. When GTA comes out, you’ll be able to jump back to your main PlayStation 5 profile, and because you’ve enabled local sharing, you’ll be able to access the game early via your own account. It’s an extra step but it’s worthwhile doing. Here’s a handy table to help you understand when you can play GTA 6 using the New Zealand trick. It’s so close now, it’s unreal: Are you going to be using the New Zealand trick to play GTA 6 earlier? Let us know your plans on the Insider Gaming Discord server . For more Insider Gaming coverage, check out whether it’s better to buy the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6 . And for even more Insider Gaming delivered directly to your inbox, sign up for our newsletter Grant has been gaming for 30+ years and in the industry for 10+. You'll probably find him playing a post-apocalyptic game or an extraction shooter somewhere.

sources.title: How To Play GTA 6 A Day Early
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto VI GTA 6 PS5 Rockstar Games Xbox Grand Theft Auto 6 isn’t out in the U.S. until November 19, but if you want to play a day early, there’s a way. Here’s what you need to do. The global launch for GTA 6 starts at 12:00 a.m. in New Zealand on November 19 , which is actually 6:00 a.m. ET on November 18 in the U.S. Yay, time zones! In order to start playing at that time, however, you’ll need to do different things depending on whether you’re playing on PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S. On Xbox Series X/S, the method for unlocking GTA 6 a day early is relatively straightforward. Just go to your settings menu, scroll down to “System,” Â and select “Language and Location.” From there, choose New Zealand and choose the option to restart your console. When it boots back up, your system will behave as if it’s in the New Zealand time zone, right down to the Microsoft store that decides when your games go live. Easy! A similar New Zealand trick is possible but not nearly as straightforward on PS5. On Sony’s console you need to create an entire new PSN account and select the country during the setup process. You then need to purchase GTA 6 through the New Zealand version of the PlayStation Store. Assuming you don’t have a bank account or credit card registered to that country, you’ll need to purchase New Zealand PSN gift cards online for the total amount ($80 for the standard edition or $100 for the deluxe version). If you already purchased a U.S. version and pre-installed, sorry, that won’t be good enough. Is buying an entire second copy worth it to you to play roughly 18 hours early? Maybe! The good news is that you don’t have to play your New Zealand version of GTA 6 only on your New Zealand PSN account. Instead, you can go to the settings menu on your NZ PSN account, open “Users and Accounts,” choose “Other,” and then select “Enable” in the “Console Sharing and Offline Play” section. This will let your regular U.S. PSN account access the game so all of your save data and trophy progress sticks with your main account. sources.name: Voxel
sources.title: Hacker que vazou gameplay de GTA 6 em 2022 se declara culpado pelo ocorrido
sources.text: GTA 6 ganha novo teaser e inicia preload após recorde de pré-vendas Arion Kurtaj, responsável pelo vazamento de quase 100 vídeos de GTA 6 em 2022 , se declarou culpado de todas as acusações relacionadas ao ataque contra os sistemas da Rockstar nesta segunda (16). O hacker, que tinha 17 anos na época, agora tem 21 e foi considerado apto a enfrentar um julgamento criminal no Reino Unido. Inicialmente, médicos haviam considerado Kurtaj inapto para participar de um julgamento tradicional e ele foi encaminhado a um hospital psiquiátrico de segurança máxima. Após uma nova avaliação, porém, o jovem foi transferido para uma prisão comum em janeiro e levado ao Tribunal da Coroa de Woolwich, onde admitiu os crimes — conforme relatado pelo BBC . Kurtaj fazia parte do grupo de hackers Lapsus$ quando invadiu os sistemas da Rockstar em 2022. Na época, ele divulgou quase 100 vídeos de gameplay e diversas capturas de tela de GTA 6 , que ainda estava em desenvolvimento e nem sequer havia recebido seu primeiro trailer oficial. O material revelou detalhes importantes sobre o jogo, incluindo a menção de uma protagonista feminina, posteriormente confirmada como Lucia. A quantidade de informações divulgadas foi tão grande que parte do público chegou a duvidar da autenticidade dos arquivos. Na época, médicos consideraram que Kurtaj não tinha condições de participar de um julgamento convencional devido à gravidade de seu autismo. Por isso, ele foi submetido a um chamado julgamento dos fatos, no qual o júri deveria avaliar se ele havia cometido os atos atribuídos a ele, sem determinar sua intenção criminosa. Em dezembro de 2023, o tribunal determinou que o hacker permanecesse internado em um hospital de segurança máxima por tempo indeterminado, a menos que médicos concluíssem que ele não representava mais um perigo. Uma avaliação posterior, realizada no fim do ano passado, considerou Kurtaj apto a responder criminalmente pelos crimes, mas ele acabou se declarando culpado de todas as acusações. O ataque à Rockstar aconteceu enquanto Kurtaj estava em liberdade sob fiança por outros crimes de hacking e recebia proteção policial. Ele estava hospedado em um hotel da rede Travelodge, em Bicester, após receber ameaças de hackers rivais relacionadas a bitcoins roubados. Como seu computador havia sido confiscado, Kurtaj utilizou um Amazon Fire Stick conectado à televisão do quarto, além de teclado e mouse Bluetooth, para acessar os sistemas internos da Rockstar. Com isso, conseguiu roubar dados da empresa, incluindo cerca de 90 vídeos que somavam quase uma hora de gameplay de GTA 6 . Depois da invasão, o hacker acessou o Slack interno da Rockstar e ameaçou divulgar o código-fonte do jogo caso a empresa não entrasse em contato com ele pelo Telegram em até 24 horas. Como a companhia não atendeu à exigência, ele publicou os arquivos em um fórum usando o nome de usuário TeaPotUberHacker . A Rockstar estimou que o ataque gerou US$ 5 milhões em custos de recuperação, além de milhares de horas de trabalho da equipe. A empresa também confirmou que o vazamento revelou antecipadamente a existência de uma protagonista feminina, informação que estava sendo mantida em sigilo para a campanha de divulgação do jogo. Arion Kurtaj não deve ser confundido com o CYBERLEEK , responsável por uma série de vazamentos de GTA 6 nos últimos meses . São episódios distintos, separados por anos e atribuídos a agentes diferentes — embora ambos envolvam informações internas do jogo da Rockstar. Os materiais atribuídos ao CYBERLEEK incluem imagens de gameplay e informações sobre sistemas que estariam presentes em GTA 6 . Entre os conteúdos divulgados estão detalhes sobre o mapa de Leonida, possíveis mecânicas de resistência e até um sistema de honra semelhante ao de Red Dead Redemption 2 . Também é importante considerar que as imagens parecem mostrar versões antigas de GTA 6 , possivelmente gravadas há mais de um ano. Portanto, recursos e mecânicas vistos nos vídeos podem ter sido modificados ou removidos pela Rockstar antes do lançamento. Após os vazamentos de 2022 e as novas divulgações atribuídas ao CYBERLEEK, GTA 6 está cada vez mais perto de chegar ao público. Ansioso para finalmente jogar o game na próxima quinta (19)? sources.text: Arion Kurtaj, the then-17-year-old hacker who allegedly leaked early Grand Theft Auto 6 footage back in 2022 after hacking into developer Rockstarâs servers, has officially pled guilty to the crime four years later. The BBC reports that the now-21-year-old pled guilty at the Woolwich Crown Court in London today, November 16, both to the Rockstar hack that leaked early in-development footage of GTA 6 , and to several other cybercrimes carried out as part of the hacking gang Lapsus$. The entire saga has been wild to watch unfold. Kurtaj first hacked into Rockstar’s servers while on bail for other crimes, and was able to do so with an Amazon Fire Stick in a hotel room while under police protection. He then posted in the companyâs Slack threatening the company if it didnât negotiate with him over Telegram. He pled not guilty in 2022. Initially, Kurtaj was deemed unfit to stand trial , with medical professionals citing his acute autism as cause to have him instead sentenced to life in a hospital prison . However, in January 2026 it was determined he was now fit to stand trial, and he subsequently pled guilty. His sentencing will be scheduled for a later date. A Message from Rockstar Games pic.twitter.com/T4Wztu8RW8 — Rockstar Games (@RockstarGames) September 19, 2022 Rockstar refused to negotiate with Kurtaj at the time, but the studio has acknowledged the entire thing over the years, with Grand Theft Auto 6 âs second trailer containing what seems to be a joke poking fun at the hack asÂ the gameâs co-lead Jason says that heâs âfixing some leaksâ while patching up a roof. This would only be the first of several leaks GTA6 would be subject to, as the game was subsequently leaked over the course of several weeks earlier this year by someone going by Cyberleek , who posted multiple clips of what seems to be an early build of the game. sources.title: Hacker behind 2022 GTA VI leaks pleads guilty
sources.text: Arion Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of GTA VI years before its release. Arion Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of GTA VI years before its release. Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other big companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS says. He was sentenced to life in a secure hospital in December 2023 because of his autism, but in January, Kurtaj was deemed fit for trial and moved to prison, the BBC reports . Kurtaj is set to be sentenced on November 23rd. GTA VI will be released on November 19th.

stories.title: The History of Grand Theft Auto Easter Eggs
stories.summary: We explore the inside jokes and little secrets tucked in every corner of the GTA maps.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: The History of Grand Theft Auto Easter Eggs
sources.text: When you’ve got an open world as big and dense as Grand Theft Auto, you’ve got to fill it with something. Restaurants, tennis courts, hidden packages, Strangers and Freaks. All kinds of treats to reward our exploration, some buried deeper than others. From hearts and minds to signs and shrines, the inside jokes and little secrets Rockstar’s calling card tucked in every corner of the map. This is the history of Grand Theft Auto easter eggs. The top-down Grand Theft Autos are too sparse and pixelated for the kind of buried treasures that would await us in the 3D era, but easter eggs exist even in this perspective. The most famous secret of the first GTA games involves lines of chanting bald NPCs dressed in orange robes, evocative of the Hare Krishna devotees famous for descending upon travelers at airports. If you can run the entire procession down sequentially, you’re rewarded with a seemingly nonsensical shout of “GOURANGA!” The phrase, a Krishna term meaning “be happy,” became the series’ signature meme among the early fanbase and resurfaced in the first few sequels, with hidden bonuses for mowing down Elvis impersonators in GTA 2 and football hooligans in GTA: London. For a series so devoted to examining the American dream, it’s easy to forget that Grand Theft Auto is British-born. The Scottish studio that created the series and the English brothers who made it a phenomenon belong to a storied Britdev tradition of taking the mick in the margins. From the ZX Spectrum emulator Rare buried in GoldenEye to Team17’s profane cheat codes and salty rants against Amiga Power magazine, British studios excel at hiding cheeky winks within their games. DMA Design, later Rockstar North, is no exception. DMA logos are disguised among the scenery, the pager randomly rags on staffers, and director Keith Hamilton himself sends you on a mission to find “the elements of GTA.” You can unlock R-rated language by naming your character after the studio’s credited “Project Bloke.” The developers are sharing their private jokes with the players, leaving their signatures in out-of-reach places. It’s been that way since the very first easter egg: The people in the game are talking to us, but they make it hard to hear them. The developers are very present in GTA 3. The game came in hot, suffered hurried changes, and still showed a lot of its arcadey roots. The veil between the game and its inner workings is thinnest here, you can out of bounds and fly the unflyable dodo across nonexistent towns named after team members. Look to La Luna through the eyes of a sniper rifle and pull the trigger to change the size of the moon, since the devs never decided how big it should be. You had to be willing to break the game a little bit to earn your peek behind the curtain, but it wasn’t that hard to do in 2001. Rockstar anticipated our escape. If you drive up a staircase near a parking lot in Staunton Island, you can hop out and use your car to climb onto a normally inaccessible roof. A precision jump drops you in an unused back alley, where you’ll find a sign that says “You weren’t supposed to be able to get here, you know.” The devs mercifully included a ramp to get us back into the game proper rather than risking a softlock. They knew we’d be snooping around. Some developers would dummy out this kind of content once it's discovered, but Rockstar maintained it as a running gag, slapping messages in hard-to-find spots throughout the series. In GTA: Vice City, Tommy can clip through a wall near the VCN helipad to enter a room with a simple marvel pedestal, upon which rests a single egg emblazoned “Happy Easter!” You’ll find no such ovoid in GTA: San Andreas. The closest you’ll come is the Gant Bridge that connects San Fierro with Las Venturas. The visitor center below contains a display serving up fun facts about the bridge. On closer inspection the text is actually information on the structure’s internal game files, like how it’s made up of 16,000 polygons and takes up a “staggering 1.27mb of disc space.” The sign was actually updated by Grove Street Games for the Definitive Edition release. After 17 years, the bridge’s triangle count doubled, the textures increased fourfold, and the disk space increased a whopping 3,000 percent. Good thing storage has stayed so affordable! If CJ can tear himself away from the field trip exhibits and land himself on top of the southern suspension tower, he’ll find another secret scolding among the orange steel rivets: “There are no Easter Eggs up here. Go away.” Clearly anticipating you’d be crushed by the disappointment of your futile search, Rockstar eases the pain with a handy parachute to get you back on your feet. Grand Theft Auto 4 does the bit, too. And cleverly, though nothing mind-blowing for the most part. A museum placard giving out about how hard the dinosaur skeletons were to sculpt, or a warning inside of the Statue of Happiness, through a door in the base reached only by air. “No hidden content,” reads an engraving by a collision-free closed door. Walk through the illusory wall, however and you’ll encounter something far more visceral than anything that’s come before. Inside you’ll find a ladder vanishing upwards into the body of the rusted copper colossus. Reach the top and you’ll find a scaffold standing just below a huge and hideous heart. Suspended painfully from chains, its maddening beat thunders inside the internal steel chamber and it cannot die. You’re not going to fit this thing in a bunny’s basket. It’s a darker, more unsettling easter egg than any that’s come before, even if it’s apparently just a jab at Hillary Clinton, who had gone after Rockstar hard as a senator during the San Andreas Hot Coffee scandal. The Heart of Liberty City is the stuff that creepypastas are made of, legends spread in schoolyards and over IRC. The series had outgrown this style of secret by the time of GTA 5. The mysterious content within its sprawling map goes far beyond the scope of eas

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker pleads guilty to all charges
sources.text: Arion Kurtaj released dozens of GTA 6 videos to the public more than a year before the game was formally revealed. The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group. Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick , a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin. A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital , where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger. As we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Kurtaj was also reportedly violent while in hospital custody, causing "dozens" of reports of injuries or property damage. In July 2026, that 'no longer a danger' determination was presumably made, as Kurtaj was released from hospital and moved to prison to await retrial. He has now pleaded guilty to multiple hacks carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, including the Rockstar hack that led to the GTA 6 leak. He also pleaded guilty to assaults on workers while in custody, which the BBC report says included "multiple biting incidents." As I said when Kurtaj was moved from hospital to prison, the whole thing strikes me as odd. The big question is how Kurtaj's state of mind at the time of the crimes will influence the outcome of his guilty plea, given that a previous court determined that he needed multiple years of institutionalization. BBC tech reporter Joe Tidy, who's been following the case since Kurtaj's transfer, also described it as "an unusual move" in his report. Coincidentially, one must assume, Grand Theft Auto 6 launches for consoles on November 19. Kurtaj will be sentenced at a future date. The leaker who goes by Cyberleek , who recently distributed several GTA 6 gameplay videos apparently taken with a development build of the game, remains at large. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
sources.text: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. It's fitting I guess that GTA San Andreas is such a strange delight to return to. As I've waited, like everyone else, for GTA 6 , I've been back here in the GTA games of the past, via the slightly dodgy remasters from a few years ago. And what's come through for me, spending a few idle mornings messing around in San Andreas, a game I thought I knew pretty well, is how beautifully odd everything is now. The best part of 20 years have given a game that once strained against its host technology a genuine aesthetic. Surprisingly sparse in detailing, as angular and sheer as dream architecture, in love with expanses, San Andreas is perfectly placed, it seems to me, to capture just how weird California can be. California and Nevada. This is the part I always forget. I mainly think of San Andreas these days through the lens of GTA 5 , which gives you LA and its surroundings but lets the single city serve as the star. It has a bigger footprint than the earlier game, sure, but it uses that space to go deep on the detailing and the sense of a singular, fiercely specific place. San Andreas meanwhile offers three cities - and one of them isn't actually in California. Alongside spins on LA and San Francisco, you get a version of Las Vegas. It's quite neat really: the three points of some arcane spiritual triangle. The kind of thing Marvel Whiteside Parsons, aerospace engineer and Actual Wizard, might have scratched in the dust of his backyard to help him control the weather. He lived - and died - in Pasadena, so all this would have been familiar anyway. There is a classic moment in every GTA. A moment where the map opens up in the early games, or when you explore enough in the later games, and simply get to understand the audacity of what is being attempted here. In San Andreas, and this feels apt, the best way to have this moment is to break the rules, sneaking into the open map before the game is fully ready for you. An early mission allows you to step away from the critical path, as it were, and peg it to the airport in Los Santos, where a plane is waiting to be pinched. Taxi, feel the thrust, and you're off. LA beneath you - sorry, Los Santos - and on the horizon a dinkytown version of the Golden Gate Bridge and the MGM Grand. Dinkytown is the word. From the sky, the huge map of San Andreas, which still feels like an incredible piece of work - such ambition! - can look like toys laid out on a duvet in the remasters. Coming back from GTA 5, a masterpiece of texture, the cities of San Andreas in particular feel very weird - cramped and condensed and wonderfully stagey, arranged the way a kid might jury-rig them together from shoeboxes and stray cardboard. On your way out of Grove Street early on you pass the Los Santos equivalent of the Hollywood sign, looming so close the way it does in the movies but not in the actual city and you feel you could touch it. Downtown is reduced to a handful of the best buildings - it's always pleasing to see the one from the brilliant first act of Speed made the cut - but still manages to capture the important stuff too, which in this case is the way that modern LA looms somewhat cruelly over the old city, captured with a strange sepulchral dignity in the form of the City Hall, so easy to spot but now so small! Elsewhere, the ersatz Las Vega Strip looks like a drawing based on memory - a few of the classic shapes are there, but it's a sketch of a place. In this way, I guess, it captures a truth about Las Vegas. Also, perhaps, it's an admission that this is a town comfortably out of the reach of satire. As for San Francisco, it's a 60s cop movie delight to fishtail around. It nails the hills and what more do you need for a game with cars in it? Taken as a whole these cities feel mesmerising now. And it's the limitations that make them sing, I think: those sheer granite canyons of downtown LA with its towering blocks of architecture and surprisingly thin traffic, with only the very faintest of ambient soundtracks that ensures any gunfire will pop and clap and shake you out of your seat. (Remember, I am playing the remasters and sound effects may be missing.) This is the LA of Repo Man rather than Heat - an otherland where the buildings feel alien, even the air feels alien. At night, palm trees stand out against a sky that glows a deep, clean red. GTA 5 would finesse all of this, the skyboxes and whatnot, but perhaps in that finessing something is lost. (Both games, incidentally, have such a talent for capturing California's kitsch excess that they perhaps miss some of the sweeter truths, such as the astonishing diversity of cultures a city like Los Angeles finds homes for. But how could any game do that justice?) Dinkytowns aside, what San Andreas does better than GTA 5 is space - the peculiar flat spaces of Southern California in particular, a state in which you can never quite tell where the wilderness ends and the landscaping begins, and where the ancient rocks that announce the horizon can look new, like stage settings, while the freeways feel truly ancient, concrete lizards sleeping on the dirt, bleached by the easy sun. I can lose hours out here. I have had to double- and triple-check that GTA 5 is the bigger game, in fact, because San Andreas still feels absolutely enormous, a trick that w

sources.title: Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director was "circling" a revival of BioWare's KOTOR for years
sources.text: "What if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games?" I imagine most BioWare fans would argue that the studio's peak happened somewhere between Dragon Age: Origins and Mass Effect 2. For me, though, the absolute high point was Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and I was always a little bitter that the devs moved on to create Mass Effect rather than finishing Revan's story in a proper KOTOR 3. That's why seeing Casey Hudson, original director of KOTOR, return with a spiritual successor in Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic is so exciting, and it's apparently been a long time coming. "It is really a dream project for us," Hudson says in an interview with The Fourth Curtain podcast . After leaving BioWare – for a second time – in 2020, he founded a new studio called Humanoid Origin, which was developing a "sci-fi action RPG" that would've been a "brand-new IP." That studio shuttered in 2024 after an "unexpected shortfall of funding," leaving Hudson to figure out what to do next. "We had lots of ideas, including, like, 'Do we get funding to continue with what we were doing? Are there other paths forward?' But over the years – myself and folks from our team, we worked on the original Knights of the Old Republic way back in the day, and since then BioWare also had the Old Republic MMO. So we've kept up connections with folks at Lucasfilm ," he says. Some time after Humanoid Origin shut down, Hudson explains, "the head of Disney Games reached out and said, 'Hey, what if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games? The spiritual successor.'" Hudson says he'd been "circling" the idea of returning to KOTOR for some time. "It's something that I would love to do, but I was either doing other things or other projects. There were times when maybe it wasn't right for Lucasfilm, or they weren't ready for it. There wasn't really a fit." He was excited both by the possibility of returning to KOTOR and bringing back "some of the the top folks we've worked with," but surviving a studio shutdown leads you to "become the most skeptical person on earth," he says. "You don't really trust anyone to follow through with a deal or funding until things are signed, done, and legit." Getting those contracts finalized is how Hudson spent "the first half" of 2025. Then he spent the rest of the year "just starting to assemble our team, doing a prototype, and then creating the announcement trailer." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Yes, that means that Fate of the Old Republic had only barely entered development at the time of its reveal at The Game Awards last year, but Hudson seems confident we won't be waiting forever for it to be finished. The team works "at a very brisk pace," and he says we should expect "new announcements" sometime next year. Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic could be going for "a more simple hero's journey" to avoid BioWare's "self-indulgent" storytelling, says ex-Dragon Age boss Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Shigeru Miyamoto to receive inaugural Legend Award at the 30th DICE Awards
sources.text: The new honor will be presented no more than once a decade Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto will be the first recipient of the Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences' new Legend Award. The AIAS said Miyamoto will be honored at the 30th annual DICE Awards, which take place at the Cosmopolitan in Las Vegas on February 18. The Legend Award is designed to recognize "an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainment," the organization said, confirming it will be presented "no more than once per decade." "Shigeru Miyamoto is widely recognized as one of the most respected and impactful figures in the games industry and beyond," said AIAS president Meggan Scavio. "We believe he perfectly embodies our inaugural Legend Award through his impact and reach, and we are so humbled and excited to have Mr. Miyamoto accept this award at the 30th anniversary of the DICE Awards." Miyamoto joined Nintendo in 1977 after studying industrial design at Kanazawa College of Art. He created Donkey Kong in 1981, and went on to develop Super Mario Bros. and The Legend of Zelda, as well as the Pikmin series, Wii Sports, and Wii Fit. He has been Nintendo's representative director and fellow since 2015, and is currently focused on bringing Nintendo's characters to theme parks and film. It isn't Miyamoto's first honor. Last month, he was announced as the first game developer to receive Japan's Order of Culture award .

sources.title: Shigeru Miyamoto to be honored with first AIAS Legend Award in Las Vegas
sources.text: Nintendo’s creative fellow will appear at DICE in February Nintendoâs creative leader, Shigeru Miyamoto, is set to be honored by The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) with its inaugural Legend Award. The Super Mario and Legend of Zelda designer will be presented with the award at a special 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony at the Cosmopolitan in Las Vegas on Thursday, February 18. According to the AIAS, the Legend Award ârecognizes an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainmentâ, honoring creators âwhose groundbreaking achievements have already earned lasting universal acclaimâ. As a “generational honor”, the award will be presented no more than once per decade, according to the Academy. Meggan Scavio, president of the AIAS, said: â Shigeru Miyamoto is widely recognized as one of the most respected and impactful figures in the games industry and beyond. “We believe he perfectly embodies our inaugural Legend Award through his impact and reach, and we are so humbled and excited to have Mr. Miyamoto accept this award at the 30th anniversary of the D.I.C.E. Awards.” Shigeru Miyamoto joined Nintendo in 1977. His first breakout project, Donkey Kong, put the company on the path to becoming a video game giant, and he later helped create many of its most popular franchises, including Mario, Zelda, and Star Fox . Miyamoto is credited with pioneering many video game conventions, including the design language for platformer and 3D action games. In 2015, he was appointed as Nintendoâs âcreative fellowâ and is one of few employees permitted to remain at the company beyond the mandatory retirement age of 65. In recent years, Miyamoto has spearheaded Nintendo’s efforts to expand its franchises beyond games, producing the Super Mario Bros. movies and overseeing the design and construction of the Super Nintendo World areas of various Universal Studios theme parks.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Original GTA 6 leaker pleads guilty to hacking Rockstar Games, years after first revealing Lucia
sources.text: The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses. The GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages. At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse. As the BBC reports , he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced. Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret. "We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar said at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way." Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up .

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Rockstar is so confident in GTA 6's weather it has The Weather Channel itself sharing screenshots
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto weather has never looked so good After repurposing Netflix for trailer playback, Rockstar has now recruited The Weather Channel to help promote GTA 6 . The institution beloved by everyone wondering if their barbecue will be rained out is now sharing screenshots of the next Grand Theft Auto, complete with new developer insights on its ambitious weather system. Oddly enough, these might be the most impressive GTA 6 screenshots so far. "Nobody knows weather like we do. That's why [ Rockstar Games ] gave us an exclusive look at the forecast for Leonida and the dynamic weather in GTAVI," reads a recent Twitter post from The Weather Channel. Rockstar's Owen Shepherd, art VP of light and rendering, examines the tech that went into GTA 6's weather system, which had the challenge of capturing the unpredictable Florida climate. "To match the fidelity of all aspects of what is the deepest, most immersive take on the Grand Theft Auto series yet, we had to completely reimagine our in-game weather systems to feel more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic," says Shepherd. "Weather can range with everything from clear blue skies to towering vertiginous cumulonimbus clouds, grounding players in a world through weather we hope Florida locals - and new visitors to Leonida - can appreciate." The six new screenshots (collected in the above gallery) show heavy rain, storm clouds brewing and striking, and – probably most convincingly – heavy mist and fog blanketing Leonida. Ask any developer who's ever optimized volumetric fog: this stuff is hard to do well without tanking performance. You can definitely see the legwork from Red Dead Redemption 2 repurposed here. GTA 6 is somewhat disappointingly targeting 30 FPS on PS5, Xbox Series X, and even PS5 Pro, but even I have to admit that Leonida's amber light filtered through the cloying sea fog is stunning. sources.title: GTA 6 Has 62 Bird Types, Confirms Rockstar Games
sources.text: Most people struggle to name more than 20 or 30 bird species. So, of course, Rockstar has gone overboard and thrown in 62 types of birds into GTA 6. They will add to the game’s incredible density, but make game completion that much harder. It would be very unRockstarlike to skimp on the details and granularity of GTA 6 ‘s world. It’s no surprise to hear then that Grand Theft Auto 6 has more bird types littered throughout the game than America has states—much more. Also, you can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here , if you haven’t already! In one of the final major previews before GTA 6’s launch, The Guardian described its experience of the game, how they interacted with the world, and explained their brief curiosity about a bird. ‘Later, I see a gull sitting on a post by the beach and ask, just to be annoying, what kind of bird it is. Jason pulls out a pair of binoculars, the gull is recorded in a wildlife logbook, and I am told with pride that there are 62 types of birds to spot.’ As we’ve already covered in our piece on how long it will take to complete GTA 6 and get the Platinum Trophy Mythic Achievement , we mentioned that it’s likely you’ll need to track down all birds—although it’s not official. 62 birds, and you just know a handful of them are super-rare and will be much harder to track down than a common bread-eating seagull! sources.title: All GTA 6 Screenshots By Rockstar Games
sources.text: Since the first GTA 6 screenshots dropped, we’ve had close to 300 screenshots for Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar Games’ marketing and advertising for GTA 6 has been special, and we’re celebrating with a full recap of all the screenshots. We got GTA 6 Trailer 1 to kickstart the hype, but Rockstar left us out in the cold for a while. It took until late 2025 and 2026 for the company to step up the marketing. This has resulted in a glitzy showreel of stunning screenshots unveiled over months. Also, you can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here , if you haven’t already! So far, 281 GTA 6 screenshots have been shown to the world through Rockstar Games’ official website, through various editorial previews and interviews for outlets, and even on social media via The Weather Channel! Screenshots have featured all sorts of gameplay elements: Jason and Lucia together, wildlife, weather systems , cars , and so much more. It’s been a long road to get to GTA 6’s release day, but it’s nearly here. First of all, huge credit goes to @GTAVI_Countdown for uploading a comprehensive compilation of every GTA 6 screenshot. Unless Rockstar treats us all to even more late additions—which you’ll hear about first at Insider Gaming as always—this looks to be the final, epic showreel of GTA 6 screenshots. The video is 4 minutes and 42 seconds long, with each screenshot getting about a second of screen time before the next one is up. There’s plenty of time to pause the video and grab screenshots of your favourite ones for screensavers or anything else.
